newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end lower on late wheat break.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end lower on late wheat break.

text.p: CBOT soybeans closed lower on a late and swift break from the day's highs in wheat, traders said.
"Wheat collapsed late and brought beans down," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Soybean futures were higher early in the day on bullish input from the export sector, a firm tone in nearby soymeal contracts and followthrough technical buying after the short-covering rally late in Friday's session, they said.
"Export inspections were very good for corn and good for beans," Kucha said.
USDA early Monday said U.S. soybeans inspected for export during the week ended November 21 totaled 32.246 million bushels, within the range of trader estimates from 27 million to 38 million bushels.
The soymeal market found support from Friday's USDA Seven State Cattle-On-Feed report, traders said.
USDA said there were 8.544 million head of cattle on feed as of November 1, up one percent from a year ago.
Soybeans closed 1-1/2 to 5-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with January down 1-1/2 at $7.08 per bushel. March was down 1-1/2 at $7.06-3/4.

There were expectations for the cattle tally to drop 1/2 percent. Also the number of cattle placed on feed during November was 2.531 million, up 11 percent from a year ago compared with expectations for a 5.7 percent rise.
Soybeans held firm early on input from the chart sector with the four- and 20-day moving averages showing bullish flags before the open Monday.

Some chartists cited first resistance in the January at $7.13 per bushel and second resistance at $7.21. The session high for January was $7.15, within the range of a key chart breakout area from $7.14 to $7.15. But buying interest Monday evaporated in that important resistance area.
First support for January was $7.04 and second support at $6.96. The session low for January was $7.07-1/2.

Some traders said soy was pressured by by a slowdown in the soybean crush pace. The National Oilseeds Processors Association said 29.683 million bushels of soybeans were crushed during the week ended November 20. That was below trader expectations for 31.0 million bushels, traders said.

Key players included Refco Inc with three million bushels bought in the January and two million in March, traders said. Options-related buying totaled one million in the January and Dean Witter Reynolds bought one million January, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 46,000 contracts, above the 41,883 traded Friday, according to the CBOT.

In soybean options, Lind Waldock sold 250 March $7.25 calls at 16 to 17 cents, Refco Inc bought 200 January $6.75 calls at 38 to 38-1/2 cents and Tenco Inc bought 200 January $7.00 puts at 5-3/4 cents, traders said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, above the 9,532 traded Friday.
